articles/2011-তাঁর-প্রভাব-আমার-জীবনে-রয়.summary: Hameeda Hossain writes about her mother, Mariam Sheikh, who grew up in Turkey during Mustafa Kemal's reforms, married young in Sindh, nursed refugees at Partition and later took up social work, and whose open mind shaped her daughters' lives.
articles/2011-তাঁর-প্রভাব-আমার-জীবনে-রয়.title_en: Her Influence Remains in My Life
articles/2011-তাঁর-প্রভাব-আমার-জীবনে-রয়.corrections: The clipping shows no newspaper name or date, so the source cannot be confirmed from the document. It is credited as a translation by Mahfuzar Rahman (অনুবাদ: মাহফুজার রহমান), so it was likely first written in English.

articles/daily-star-2004-salma's-journey.summary: An In Memoriam tribute to Salma Sobhan a year after her death, tracing her path from Pakistan's first woman barrister and Dhaka law teacher through Forum, 1971 and BILIA to co-founding Ain o Salish Kendra and its legal aid and eviction work.

articles/daily-star-2005-killing-field-o.summary: Written after the Spectrum factory building collapsed at Palashbari, Savar, on 11 April 2005, the article questions the official count of dead and missing workers. It argues the deaths amount to culpable homicide and calls for an independent investigation, prosecution and proper compensation.

articles/daily-star-2008-are-we-serious-.summary: On CEDAW's 29th anniversary, she reviews Bangladesh's record ahead of its sixth report. She presses for withdrawing reservations to Articles 2 and 16.1(c), enacting a domestic violence law, amending the Citizenship Act and holding direct elections to women's reserved seats.

articles/New Age-2007-rationalising labo.summary: Writing as convenor of the Workers Safety Forum, she sets the garment industry's export growth against stagnant minimum wages, repeated factory fires, weak inspection and the 2006 worker unrest. She calls for safe workplaces, legal rights, housing and transport instead of force.
articles/New Age-2007-rationalising labo.corrections: Date (Friday, 18 May 2007) is confirmed, but the clipping does not show the newspaper name: it is a page headed "Make Trade Fair Alliance" (ন্যায্য বাণিজ্য জোট), so "New Age" cannot be confirmed from the document.

articles/Prothom-Alo-2008-amra-jodi-shot.summary: The Bangla version of her CEDAW anniversary article, published in Prothom Alo's human rights section. It asks the government to withdraw its reservations, pass a domestic violence law, reform citizenship law and allow direct election of women to reserved parliamentary seats.
articles/Prothom-Alo-2008-amra-jodi-shot.title_en: If We Truly Want the CEDAW Convention Implemented

articles/prothom-alo-2016-narir-jonno-pr.summary: Part of a New Year feature in which four contributors set out hopes for women in 2016. Her piece looks back over 40 years of change, low wages for women workers, unrecognised domestic work, the child marriage age debate and continuing sexual violence.
articles/prothom-alo-2016-narir-jonno-pr.corrections: "নারীর জন্য প্রত্যাশা" is the title of the whole page (Narimancha, p. 14, Tuesday 5 January 2016). Her own piece is titled "আমরা কি নিজেদের বঞ্চনার কথা বলতে পারছি?" (Are we able to speak of our own deprivation?).
articles/prothom-alo-2016-narir-jonno-pr.people: Other contributors on the page: Salma Ali, Farah Kabir, Tanjib ul Alam

articles/New-Nation-1991-Political optio.summary: A two-part article reporting a Gonotantrik Uddyog survey of 522 candidates before the 1991 parliamentary election. It compares party positions on parliamentary government, Islam as state religion, the military, the Chittagong Hill Tracts, foreign aid, the Gulf War and women's rights.
articles/New-Nation-1991-Political optio.corrections: Published in two parts, "Political options in a democratic society-I" (24 February 1991) and "-II" (25 February 1991), as the handwritten dates show.

articles/The Independent-2000-The Way ah.summary: Her contribution to an International Women's Day supplement looks at rising dowry violence, rape, domestic violence and acid attacks, using ASK figures for 1996 to 1998. She discusses shalish, police failures and the need for legal and social remedies.
articles/The Independent-2000-The Way ah.corrections: "The way ahead for equality between men and women in Bangladesh" is the headline of the supplement page (p. 14, sponsored by CIDA). Her article itself is headed "Challenging Violence".

articles/daily-star-2005-womens-rights-i.summary: She warns that the 2004 National Policy for Women's Advancement rolled back the 1997 policy's commitments on equal rights to property, land and inheritance, alongside indirect selection of reserved-seat MPs. She urges women across parties to campaign against the backslide.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=atnunRcF.summary: A short 1947 Partition Archive video in which she recalls her childhood in Sindh: her father, a judge who educated his daughters, a school emptied of Hindu, Sikh and Christian pupils after Partition, and helping at her grandmother's refugee clinic.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=atnunRcF.corrections: YouTube title is "Dr. Hameeda Hossain lived in Hyderabad, Sindh, during 1947", uploaded 16 May 2012 by the 1947PartitionArchive channel. The page does not name the interviewer or recording date, so Farhana Afroz and February 2012 could not be checked.

https://mittalsouthasiainstitute.harvard.summary: Transcript of a panel at the Mittal Institute's Bangladesh at 50 conference. She argues that women's gains in education, work and visibility over 50 years are uneven across class, ethnicity, location and religion, and traces how women organised against discrimination and violence.
https://mittalsouthasiainstitute.harvard.corrections: The panel took place on 3 March 2021, during the virtual "Bangladesh @ 50: Looking Back, Looking Forward" conference (3 to 4 March 2021). The Harvard site blocked direct access; it was read from a Wayback Machine copy.
https://mittalsouthasiainstitute.harvard.people: Moderator Marty Chen; co-panelists Shireen Huq, Naila Kabeer, Khushi Kabir

https://web.archive.org/web/202407231221.summary: A long oral history covering her childhood in Sindh, Wellesley, publishing work, editing Forum in 1960s Dhaka, the events of March 1971, return to Bangladesh in 1972, Oxford research on Bengal weavers, exile after 1975, Karika and founding ASK.
https://web.archive.org/web/202407231221.corrections: The Tufts catalogue record (dl.tufts.edu/concern/audios/ht24x021b) gives the date only as 2011 and names no interviewer, so "Iftekhar Iqbal" and "January 20, 2011" could not be confirmed. Summary is based on the Tufts transcript, not on listening to the audio.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9wArB1Po.summary: A video interview from Dhaka recorded by Marieme Helie Lucas for the Secularism Is A Women's Issue series, part of a set of conversations with feminists on secularism, fundamentalisms and women's rights.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9wArB1Po.corrections: The YouTube title is "Women speak on secularism from . . . Dhaka, Bangladesh, Hameeda Hossain (January 8, 2012)", while the description says it was recorded in April 2011. Uploaded 3 December 2012 by the sacwbackend channel.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cgoizwmc.summary: An episode of the Desh TV conversation programme Bela Obela Sarabela in which Hameeda Hossain talks with actor and politician Asaduzzaman Noor.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cgoizwmc.title_en: Bela Obela Sarabela (Morning, Noon and Night)
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cgoizwmc.corrections: YouTube upload date is 20 November 2021 (US Pacific time), which is 21 November in Bangladesh, so the listed date is consistent. Channel: Desh TV Entertainment.

interviews/1994-ISIS international Women.summary: In this Q&A she describes founding Ain o Salish Kendra in 1986, its legal aid and Law and Policy Reform Forum, its response to extremist attacks on women and NGOs and to village stonings over adultery, and her own path from Pakistan to Bangladesh.
interviews/1994-ISIS international Women.corrections: The full title is "Interview: Hameeda Hossain of ASK or the Ain O Salish Kendra Law and Mediation Center, Dhaka, Bangladesh", in Women in Action 4/94 (Isis International); it notes it is taken from "Against All Odds", p. 59.

interviews/Prokriti 15 january 1998.pdf.summary: A cover feature naming five women of the year, including Matia Chowdhury, Salma Khan, Shamsera Hasan and Ferdousi Majumdar. In her section she talks about handlooms and women in the textile trade, and ASK research on laid-off garment workers, migrant women, family law and violence.
interviews/Prokriti 15 january 1998.pdf.title_en: Most Talked-About Women of the Year
interviews/Prokriti 15 january 1998.pdf.corrections: This is a cover feature on five women, not a single interview. The issue is dated January 1998 (the file name gives 15 January 1998).
interviews/Prokriti 15 january 1998.pdf.people: Written by Shahnaz Munni and Rajib Noor

interviews/Chutir Din Prothom Alo - 18 S.summary: A profile in Prothom Alo's weekly Chutir Din magazine that follows her life from Sindh and Wellesley to Dhaka, Forum, 1971, Oxford and the founding of ASK, alongside her work on slum evictions, legal aid and CEDAW reporting.
interviews/Chutir Din Prothom Alo - 18 S.title_en: Hameeda Hossain's Mission: Law for People's Welfare
interviews/Chutir Din Prothom Alo - 18 S.corrections: Full date is 18 September 2004, in Chutir Din, the weekly magazine of Prothom Alo.

interviews/INTERVIEW BY ZOFEEN T. EBRAHI.summary: In this interview she discusses religion in politics, ASK's legal work, the case for a uniform family code, her years editing Forum and in 1971, and ASK's drop-in centres for working children and the garment-industry child labour agreement.
interviews/INTERVIEW BY ZOFEEN T. EBRAHI.corrections: The document shows no publication name or date. It refers to ASK having been formed 11 years earlier, which suggests about 1997, but this is an inference and not a printed date.

interviews/Prothom Alo 26 March 2009- mu.summary: An Independence Day roundtable in Prothom Alo on hopes of the Liberation War that remain unmet. The participants discuss the constitution, democracy, secularism and the place of women since 1971.
interviews/Prothom Alo 26 March 2009- mu.title_en: The Unfulfilled Hopes of the Liberation War
interviews/Prothom Alo 26 March 2009- mu.corrections: Full date is 26 March 2009. It is a roundtable discussion with three participants and a moderator, not a solo interview.
interviews/Prothom Alo 26 March 2009- mu.people: Zillur Rahman Siddiqui; Maj. Gen. (retd) Amin Ahmed Chowdhury, Bir Bikram; moderated by Sajjad Sharif

interviews/Daily Star-May 6 2021-lot mor.summary: Interviewed after receiving the BDI Lifetime Achievement Award, she looks back on the Yasmin and Noorjahan cases, factory disasters such as Tazreen and Rana Plaza, and the rights of garment, farm and domestic workers.
interviews/Daily Star-May 6 2021-lot mor.corrections: Full headline is "We still have a lot more to do for equality". Published 6 May 2021 on The Daily Star's opinion page.

interviews/Ittefaq-29 Nov 2017-manobdhik.summary: A profile in Ittefaq's Pathikrit (Pathfinder) feature covering her childhood in Hyderabad, Sindh, Wellesley, Oxford University Press, Forum, Karika, the founding of ASK and her books, including The Company Weavers of Bengal and No Better Option?
interviews/Ittefaq-29 Nov 2017-manobdhik.title_en: A Journey to Establish Human Rights
interviews/Ittefaq-29 Nov 2017-manobdhik.corrections: The byline is Sabrina Mili (সাবরিনা মিলি), not "Sarbina Simi". Published Wednesday 29 November 2017, p. 21, in the "Pathikrit" section.

https://www.thedailystar.net/lifestyle/i.summary: For International Women's Day 2020 she discusses feminism as a struggle for justice across class and ethnicity, misogyny, reporting of violence, indirectly chosen women MPs, unenforced laws such as on harassment committees, and the role of the media.
https://www.thedailystar.net/lifestyle/i.corrections: The Daily Star page shows publication on 2 March 2020 (updated 3 March 2020).

https://bdiusa.org/wp-content/uploads/20.summary: Published after she received BDI's 2021 Lifetime Achievement Award, this interview covers her education in Sindh and at Wellesley, journalism and Forum, ASK, her writing, work against violence on women, her weavers research and her view of Bangladesh at 50.
https://bdiusa.org/wp-content/uploads/20.corrections: Interview date of 26 December 2021 is confirmed. The issue is labelled Fall 2021, but the editor's note is dated 20 January 2022. The issue also reprints her Daily Star op-ed "Women's Movement: The Challenge of Change" (26 March 2021).

magazines/মেয়েদের নির্যাতনের কেসগুলো ক.summary: A Women's Day interview in which she discusses patriarchy and violence against women, sexual harassment, fatwa cases, weak policing and courts that let cases lapse, family-based politics that does not empower women, and the organised women's movement.
magazines/মেয়েদের নির্যাতনের কেসগুলো ক.title_en: "Cases of Violence Against Women Somehow Get Deactivated"
magazines/মেয়েদের নির্যাতনের কেসগুলো ক.corrections: The magazine is Saptahik Kagoj (সাপ্তাহিক কাগজ, Weekly Kagoj), Year 4, No. 6, 4 March 2012, pp. 13 to 16, not "Canvas". The title should be the interview headline "মেয়েদের নির্যাতনের কেসগুলো কোনো না কোনোভাবে ডিএকটিভেট হয়ে যায়".
magazines/মেয়েদের নির্যাতনের কেসগুলো ক.people: Shariful Islam Polash and Aman Abdullah

magazines/Dhaka letter (mainstream June.summary: Her "Dhaka Letter" for an Indian weekly describes the May 1986 parliamentary election under General Ershad, with organised violence, booth capture and manipulated results as the Jatiyo Party sought a two-thirds majority to indemnify martial law.
magazines/Dhaka letter (mainstream June.corrections: Title should be "Dhaka Letter: Democracy at Gunpoint"; source is Mainstream (New Delhi weekly), Vol. XXIV No. 40, 7 June 1986, pp. 7 to 8. It is an article by her, not an interview.
